title: Seaweed Soup
summary: Fry the sea mustard and the beef in toasted sesame oil properly before you add the water. That is what turns the broth milky.
intro:
If your seaweed soup comes out clear and bland, the most likely reason is that you did not fry it long enough. The sea mustard and beef need at least 5 minutes in toasted sesame oil so that the fat and the seaweed's own substance dissolve into the water and the broth turns milky.

The water always goes in after the frying.
steps: Soak the dried sea mustard in cold water for 20 minutes. It swells to more than five times its size, so use a generous bowl.
Rinse the soaked seaweed two or three times to wash out the salt, squeeze it dry and cut it into 4 cm (1 1/2 in) lengths.
Cut the beef into bite-sized pieces and blot it with kitchen paper if there is a lot of blood.
Heat the sesame oil in a pot and fry the beef over medium heat. When the outside has turned pale, add the seaweed.
Keep frying the seaweed and beef together for 5 minutes. It is ready when the seaweed has turned deep green and is starting to stick to the bottom of the pot.
Add 1 Tbsp (15 mL) of the soup soy sauce and fry for another 30 seconds.
Pour in 1.5 L (6 1/4 cups) water and bring to the boil over high heat. Once it boils, skim off the foam and turn the heat down to medium-low.
Half-cover the pot and simmer for 25 minutes. When the seaweed is soft, add the minced garlic and give it another 5 minutes.
Season to taste with the remaining soup soy sauce and salt.
tips: Once soaked, 20 g (3/4 oz) of dried sea mustard is enough to fill four people. If this is your first time, start with less.
If you use clams or mussels instead of beef, you can skip the frying step: put them into boiling water and 10 minutes is enough.
The seaweed is softer the next day. There is no harm in making a big pot.
